slot.brief: Ask to rank given alkenes by heat of hydrogenation (most stable = least exothermic).

stem: Arrange the following alkenes in increasing order of stability: (I) ethene, (II) propene, (III) trans-but-2-ene, (IV) 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene.

verdicts.working: Alkene stability generally increases with alkyl substitution: ethene < propene < trans-but-2-ene < 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene.

working:
Alkene stability increases with the number of alkyl substituents on the double-bond carbons and with trans geometry. Ethene has 0 substituents, propene has 1, trans-but-2-ene has 2 and is trans, 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene has 4. Thus the order is I < II < III < IV.

Independent check: Alkene stability generally increases with alkyl substitution: ethene < propene < trans-but-2-ene < 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene.
solution: Alkene stability increases with alkyl substitution; trans geometry further stabilizes the alkene. The number of alkyl substituents increases from ethene (0) to propene (1), trans-but-2-ene (2), and 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene (4): $$\boxed{\mathrm{I<II<III<IV}}$$
